messages:
Anna Li: @here Quick heads-up — billing update going out EOD. TL;DR: invoice line bands are changing, we’re introducing a 30-day soft grace for small overages (opt-in), and we’re rolling out rate-band smoothing to reduce bill volatility for bursty customers. Details below.

Marcus Chen: Can you spell out what 'rate-band smoothing' means for throttling and rate limits? Does this change quota enforcement?

Anna Li: Good Q. Smoothing is purely pricing-side (how we map usage to invoice bands) — it does NOT relax runtime quota enforcement or rate limits. Runtime SLOs/quotas stay the same. The smoothing algorithm aggregates short bursts into a rollover bucket for billing granularity so customers don't see huge step-changes on one big spike.

Priya Nair: How small are "small overages" for the 30-day grace? Auto-applied?

Anna Li: Overages <= $250 in a billing period are eligible for a 30-day soft grace. That means the invoice will include the overage line but we won't trigger immediate collection actions for 30 days while we surface reconciliation options (credit, refund, or payment). It is auto-applied to standard hosted customers; enterprise / Dedicated / Private get manual outreach and can opt out. There is also an opt-in knob if an account prefers to defer (flag: `billing.grace_opt_in`).

Marcus Chen: Does this affect sample invoice layout or line items for customers (we need to update the Console/UI copy + sample CSV)?

Anna Li: Yes — invoice layout will show a new "Smoothed usage bands" section and a short explanation. Sample CSV and the Console preview will be updated. Example of a generated invoice line block: 

```
Account: ACCT-01234
Period: 2026-04-01 — 2026-04-30
Line items:
  - Smoothed usage band: 0-10,000,000 tokens @ $0.00050 = $5,000.00
  - Smoothed usage band: 10,000,001-100,000,000 tokens @ $0.00045 = $40,500.00
  - Burst adjustment (smoothed): -$120.00
  - Overage (soft-grace eligible): $80.00
  - Total due: $45,460.00
```

Anna Li: The sample above shows the burst adjustment row which is the output of the smoothing algorithm (can be positive or negative depending on pattern). We’ll include a short line item code so it's easy to reconcile programmatically.

Emma K: For customers who dispute an overage during the 30d grace, what's the ops flow?

Anna Li: Customer Success will get a flag on the account with recommended actions (credit vs investigate). Ops can issue a provisional credit while we investigate. If dispute unresolved after 30 days, usual collection/credit rules apply. We’ll keep logs and attach the smoothing snapshot used to compute the invoice.

Carlos M: Legal has reviewed and signed off on the revised TOS language for the soft grace + smoothing explanation. We added a short-risk clause for sustained abuse.

Priya Nair: Will this require changes to Alerting/Cost-SLAs dashboards?

Anna Li: Yes, Alerting will get two new metrics: `billing.smoothed_usage` and `billing.burst_adjustment`. We'll add a default alert for large negative adjustments (possible billing bug) and a recommended dashboard tile for Customer Success.

BillingBot: New invoice preview batch generated for sandbox accounts. Samples available at https://console.redwood.ai/billing/previews (token-limited). :page_facing_up:

Marcus Chen: Nice. Ops/Dev note — we should add the smoothing seed to the invoice metadata so we can reproduce numbers from logs.

Anna Li: Agreed. Invoice metadata will include `smoothing_seed` and `band_version`.

Emma K: One last thing — will credits/refunds still be manual?

Anna Li: Refunds/credits remain controlled by Finance. The new workflow just surfaces recommended credit amounts and marks accounts as 'soft-grace' in the ledger. For automated tiny credits (< $5) we will consider auto-apply in a follow-up (not in this rollout).

Priya Nair: Rollout schedule?

Anna Li: Rollout plan:
 - Week 0 (next Tue): Feature flags on for internal sandbox and staging; sample invoices published.
 - Week 1: Gradual rollout to 10% of paid hosted accounts; Console previews enabled.
 - Week 2: Default apply to all paid hosted accounts; manual outreach to enterprise customers.
 - Week 4: Full rollout + CSV/email template push.

Marcus Chen: OK, I'll schedule an Eng check-in after the sandbox run.

Carlos M: Thx — legal will monitor any edge disputes and loop in OPS if needed.

Anna Li: Thanks everyone — we’ll post the official external announcement copy by EOD and attach the sample CSV + FAQ. Please DM me if you want early access to the sandbox previews. :pray:
